- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap), check sentiment history: if sentiment is rising, model may be “too pessimistic”; increase forecast by 1–3%.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome (e.g., >10% gap), sentiment is likely negative or neutral; reduce forecast by 1–3% and consider mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum (last 5–7 days of true outcome); weight recent 7-day true values more heavily in forecast calibration.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values before applying correction.
